# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to establish contact and share what I see. Since Blind can't perceive gestures or writing, I can only reach Blind through speech directly (which lands on Blind and Mute in this turn since I speak last, but actually I'm last in order - Mute, Blind, Deaf - so nobody hears me this round from within the round, but they'll get it next round). Let me report clearly what's on the display.

I should describe the bomb state precisely: display shows 1, light is orange, and there are 7 wires with specific colors in specific positions. This is critical info for Mute (who has the manual and needs to match instructions to wire colors/positions) and Blind (who will need to act on wires but can't see colors, so must rely on my count/position description).

Let me speak this clearly, using position numbers since Blind can feel wire positions even if not colors.

```
speak(text="Display shows the number 1. Light is orange. There are 7 wires in order: position 1 white, position 2 blue, position 3 orange, position 4 red, position 5 purple, position 6 yellow, position 7 green.")
wait()
```

TURN 2

DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

Mute has gestured 7 blanks-worth of symbol ☝ repeated seven times to me. Since I can see gestures, I receive the actual symbols: seven ☝ in a row. This likely corresponds to something about the 7 wires — perhaps Mute is asking me to confirm each wire one by one, or indicating "look at wire" for each of the 7 positions, or counting up 1 through 7 as a sequence marker.

Since ☝ often means "point up" / "one" / "this one", repeated seven times might just be Mute acknowledging or asking me to enumerate each wire again individually, or it could be Mute's way of saying "wire 1, wire 2, ... wire 7" wanting confirmation per position rather than all at once (maybe manual requires per-wire query).

I already gave full info last turn. I'll wait to see if Blind or Mute asks something more specific, but since it's my turn now I should respond usefully. I'll re-confirm the wire list per-position since that seems to be what's being requested, and also mention I'm ready for specific questions.

```
speak(text="Confirming again in order: wire 1 white, wire 2 blue, wire 3 orange, wire 4 red, wire 5 purple, wire 6 yellow, wire 7 green. Display is 1, light is orange. If you need me to check something specific on the bomb, tell me and I will describe it.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[blue] 3:[orange] 4:[red] 5:[purple] 6:[yellow] 7:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]

Mute now gestured seven ☝ symbols plus a 👍 at the end. This still looks like counting through 7 items followed by a thumbs-up, possibly meaning "yes, confirmed" or "that's correct, proceed" — acknowledging my wire list was correct and matches the manual somehow. Or it could be building toward a specific instruction using gesture as a fallback since Mute cannot speak to me... wait, Mute CAN speak, and speech reaches me. But Mute hasn't spoken - only gestured. That's odd since gestures to me don't carry words, only shapes.

Actually, rereading: Mute cannot touch the bomb but CAN speak (only Blind and Deaf cannot speak... wait let me check: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb". So Mute cannot speak at all! Mute can only gesture. That changes everything - Mute must communicate via gestures alone, which I can see but Blind cannot.

So Mute is trying to tell me something using gestures, since gesture is Mute's only channel. Seven ☝ then 👍 might be Mute confirming "yes, all 7 wires match" or building a number/selection. Since I can't ask questions back easily except via speech to Mute (which Mute cannot hear either - Mute has no hearing restriction listed... wait, only Deaf cannot hear. Mute isn't stated to be unable to hear. Let me check: Mute "Cannot: Speak, or touch". So Mute CAN hear and CAN see gestures presumably not stated, but Mute reads the manual - sight not restricted for Mute either.

So Mute can hear me, see gestures from Deaf presumably, but cannot speak or touch. So I can speak to Mute and Mute understands, but Mute must reply only in gestures.

Given seven ☝ plus thumbs-up, likely means: "wires 1 through 7, all confirmed/correct" — an acknowledgment. I'll ask Mute a direct yes/no question they can answer with single gestures, to make communication efficient.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, thumbs up received. Does the manual say to cut a specific wire by position number? If yes, gesture the number as that many taps of one symbol, or use finger-count gestures 1 through 7 for the position.")
wait()
```

Since Blind cannot see gestures, all this exchange between me and Mute is invisible to Blind - which is fine since Blind needs to act on wires by touch and needs word instructions.

I think Mute is stuck communicating complex info only via gestures which are very limited (just symbols, no compound meaning). I should try a more direct approach: ask yes/no questions using distinct single gestures for yes/no, since Mute already used 👍 for confirmation once.

Let me propose a protocol: I'll ask if manual instruction depends on the light color (orange) - Mute can answer with 👍 or 👎.

